system_description.narrative_title: U.S. economic offensive on Iran and its ripple effects
system_description.narrative_summary: A coordinated U.S. push to impose broad, secondary economic sanctions on Iran — described by the administration as 'economic warfare' or an 'economic D-Day' — is the dominant theme. The policy aims to choke Iran's trade lifelines (oil, shipping, financial channels) and pressures partner hubs (Dubai, China), while Tehran threatens maritime retaliation in the Strait of Hormuz and other escalatory military options. Markets, insurers and regional states are already realigning: oil and equity volatility, fewer ships transiting Hormuz, and diplomatic manoeuvres as neighbours and trading partners weigh exposure. The window frames a cascading, open-system interaction among sanction policy, Iran's adaptive responses, energy flows, regional security, and global market/financial networks.
system_description.scope: Inside: U.S. sanctions policy and enforcement mechanisms (primary and secondary sanctions), Iran's economy and politico-military decision-making, maritime security and transit through the Strait of Hormuz (tankers, shipping routes, insurance), the role of trade and financial hubs (Dubai, China, Oman, Iraq), global oil flows and commodity market reactions, and immediate diplomatic/military alignments and responses by regional actors.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical order and international political economy—centered on energy security, sanctions regimes, and great-power competition.
adjacent_subsystems: Middle East regional security architecture (Gulf states, Iran, maritime chokepoints)
International sanctions and global financial/commodity trading networks
East Asian security dynamics (North Korea, South Korea, China relations)

variables.name: Sanctions scope
variables.description: The breadth of sanction measures applied extraterritorially, measured by the range of economic sectors, actors and transactions targeted.

variables.name: Enforcement intensity
variables.description: The rigor and frequency of enforcement actions and compliance checks applied to implement sanctions.

variables.name: Third‑party compliance rate
variables.description: The aggregated propensity of external economic actors and intermediaries to comply with or acquiesce to secondary sanctions.

variables.name: Sanctions circumvention activity
variables.description: The volume and sophistication of activities and networks used to evade or bypass sanctions (e.g., reflagging, front entities, opaque transactions).

variables.name: Oil transit volume
variables.description: The throughput of crude oil and refined products transiting the principal maritime chokepoints measured as volume per time.

variables.name: Global oil supply balance
variables.description: The net balance between global oil supply and demand that determines headroom and sensitivity to regional disruptions.

variables.name: Maritime security level
variables.description: The aggregate level of naval and security presence, surveillance and interdiction capability in key sea lanes.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premia
variables.description: The price level of insurance and war-risk premia charged for commercial shipping operating in the affected maritime regions.

variables.name: Vessel transit delay rate
variables.description: The rate of additional delays, rerouting and time-in-transit experienced by commercial vessels in response to risk or restrictions.

variables.name: Market volatility level
variables.description: The amplitude of price and return volatility across energy, equity and credit markets tied to regional risk perceptions.

variables.name: Investor risk positioning
variables.description: The aggregate directional exposure and hedging stance of investors to assets sensitive to regional sanctions and conflict.

variables.name: Trade‑hub dependency
variables.description: The degree to which intermediary trade and finance hubs depend on trade flows and services that are vulnerable to sanctions pressure.

variables.name: Financial channel connectivity
variables.description: The strength and opacity of banking, payments and alternative financial channels linking the targeted economy to global markets.

variables.name: Politico‑military escalation pressure
variables.description: The internal and external pressures on decision makers that raise the propensity to employ military or coercive responses.

variables.name: Energy market liquidity
variables.description: The depth and immediacy with which energy commodity markets can absorb trades without large price dislocations.

variables.name: Diplomatic coordination
variables.description: The degree of aligned diplomatic posture and cooperative action among external actors regarding sanctions, mediation or de‑escalation.

catalysts.title: U.S. Treasury broadens secondary sanctions
catalysts.description: A formal Treasury announcement widening the scope of secondary sanctions and naming additional targets, expanding extraterritorial measures.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Treasury Secretary to announce Iran sanctions", "US to broaden scope of secondary sanctions on Iran".

catalysts.title: Spike in Iranian attacks and seizures in Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Sustained Iranian maritime campaign of tanker strikes, fines and vessel seizures that degrades safe passage through Hormuz.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "New Tanker Strike in Hormuz", "Iran threatens 45 tankers", "Iran vows retaliation for U.S. economic offensive".

catalysts.title: Chinese retaliatory/countermeasure response
catalysts.description: Beijing signals potential retaliation or protective measures for partners, undermining U.S. extraterritorial pressure and enabling alternative channels.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "China warns US it could retaliate over Iran sanctions", "signals China not exempt" from US plan.

catalysts.title: Oman foreign minister visit to Tehran
catalysts.description: Scheduled Omani diplomatic visit to discuss shipping routes and mine-clearing cooperation with Iran, potentially easing regional transit risks.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Oman foreign minister to visit Tehran" and "Iran and Oman discuss joint shipping route and mine clearing mission".

catalysts.title: U.S. returns diplomats to Middle East embassies
catalysts.description: Planned redeployment of U.S. diplomatic staff to regional posts after prior evacuations, changing on‑the‑ground coordination and messaging.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "US prepares to send diplomats back to Middle East embassies after Iran war evacuations."

catalysts.title: Wave of designations against oil traders and intermediaries
catalysts.description: Ongoing US designation campaign targeting traders, tankers and intermediaries (e.g., Wellbred), likely to continue and expand enforcement.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "United States sanctions oil trader Wellbred"; coverage of broader designation campaign and 'Operation Economic Outcast'.

catalysts.title: Commercial rerouting and Arctic route tests
catalysts.description: Increased testing and use of alternative routes (including Arctic) by shippers and states to avoid Hormuz risk, altering transit times and flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "South Korea ship to test Arctic commercial route" and reports of fewer ships transiting Hormuz, Iraqi tankers' passages.
